title: Row contextual announcements and smart filter recommendations for virtual tables
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Add lightweight row-level contextual announcements and an inline smart-filter suggestion system to virtualized table components. Goal is to help users recover context when virtualized rows jump during updates and to accelerate common filter creation without overwhelming toolbar real estate.
background: Virtualized tables in the design system currently perform well for large datasets but suffer from two recurring UX issues: (1) when rows are added/removed or the table reflows, keyboard or screen-reader users can lose context because the virtualized DOM changes; (2) building filters for common queries requires opening a separate filter panel or constructing multi-step chip operations, which is a common pain reported in support tickets and research sessions.
design_goals: Provide low-cost, a11y-friendly row announcements that convey minimal context when a focused row moves or is replaced
Surface 1–3 smart filter suggestions based on visible column data and recent user actions
Keep visual surface minimal so existing dense and compact density modes are unaffected
Ensure compatibility with existing keyboard navigation and screen-reader flows
Make suggestions opt-in and easy to dismiss; avoid noisy recommendations
proposed_solution: Row-context hint: when a focused row is removed or virtualization causes the focused index to shift, emit a short ARIA live message like 'Row 14 of 120 — Title: "Payment failed" — moved to row 13'
Lightweight visual cue: a subtle transient badge on the new focused row (2s) indicating change origin (added/removed/moved)
Smart-filter suggestions: after a column header filter is opened, show up to 3 contextually ranked suggestions (e.g., top values, recently used values, suggested ranges)
Suggestion CTA: each suggestion is a tappable chip that inserts a filter expression and triggers a soft preview of filtered results without committing (preview mode)
Accessibility: ARIA roles for suggestions, keyboard support (arrow + enter to select, escape to dismiss), and screen-reader-friendly labels
Config flags: design system exposes optional props: enableRowAnnouncements, suggestionSources (top_values | recent | heuristic), suggestionLimit
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration components exist in the design repo with docs and knobs for enableRowAnnouncements and suggestionSources
Automated accessibility tests validate ARIA live announcements for the three major change types (added/removed/moved)
Keyboard-only flows allow opening suggestions, navigating suggestions, and applying/previewing without a mouse
Visual regression tests pass for compact, default, and spacious density modes (no layout shifts beyond intended transient badge)
UX research validation: 6 participants complete a context-recovery task and a filter-creation task with >80% success and qualitative reduction in confusion
Engineering integration demo using the table wrapper with a 10k-row dataset shows no measurable rendering throughput regression (within 5% of baseline)
Docs include examples, recommended heuristics for suggestionSources, and guidance for product teams on opt-in trade-offs
implementation_notes: Prefer non-blocking ARIA live region updates (aria-live='polite') to avoid interrupting screen readers
Announce only when focus exists inside table; avoid emitting messages on background sync operations
For virtualization, compute a stable pseudo-index mapping so announcements reflect user-facing row numbers (1..N) rather than DOM indices
Suggestion heuristic: combine column top-k values (client-side sample) with a short LRU of recent filter values sent from host app via table props
Preview mode implementation: apply a transient filter layer on the client side that can be toggled off without mutating central query state
Add telemetry hooks for suggestion acceptance and dismiss events to tune heuristics over time
Keep DOM additions minimal: reuse existing header filter popover container and append suggestion chips rather than creating new major overlays
risks: Too many announcements could overwhelm screen-reader users — mitigated by rate-limiting and focusing on focused-row changes only
Smart suggestions may surface sensitive or noisy values — mitigated via allowlist/denylist and product opt-in
Preview mode could cause confusion if apps have side-effectful filters — require product integration guidance and default to read-only preview unless explicitly enabled
Performance: computing heuristics on very wide tables could add CPU overhead — mitigate by sampling and background throttling
test_plan: Accessibility validation with axe-core and manual NVDA/VoiceOver checks for dynamic announcements
End-to-end tests that simulate row add/remove and verify live messages and visual badges
Performance benchmark with 10k rows and typical virtualization window to confirm <5% overhead
User session replay checks to ensure suggestion telemetry events are recorded
UX study: moderated remote sessions with 6 participants (2 keyboard-only, 2 screen-reader users, 2 mouse/touch)
